sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Collierville?
sections.html:
A Collierville homeowner owes two bills: one from the Town of Collierville and one from Shelby County. The town's tax department answers questions at 901-457-2281 or propertytax@colliervilletn.gov, and the town's Taxes page reminds residents that they also pay Shelby County taxes.

On the county side, the Shelby County Assessor of Property sets the value, the Board of Commissioners sets the county rate, and the Trustee prints and mails the notices to the address the Assessor has on file. If a mortgage lender pays your taxes from escrow, the lender may request the figures and pay, and the Trustee suggests you keep the original notice for your own records.

Because the notice goes to the address on record with the Assessor, a seller who has moved out should confirm that address before October. Missing mail does not cancel the debt.

sections.h2: What is the Collierville tax rate and how is a bill figured?
sections.html:
The town's Taxes page gives its rate as $1.62 for each $100 of assessed value. Residential property in Tennessee is assessed at 25% of appraised value, so each $100,000 of appraisal produces $25,000 of assessed value and $405.00 of Town of Collierville tax.

The same page lists the other assessment ratios the state uses: 40% for commercial and industrial property, 55% for public utilities, 25% for farms and 30% for personal property. Add the Shelby County rate, which the Trustee or Assessor can give you, to see the full bill. Applied to a $485,900 house, which is the Census Bureau's median owner-occupied value for the town, the town portion alone would be about $1,968.

The math runs like this: $485,900 times 25% gives $121,475 in assessed value, divided by 100 and multiplied by $1.62.

sections.h2: When are Collierville property taxes due and when do they go delinquent?
sections.html:
Shelby County taxes become due on the first Monday of October and can be paid without interest until the end of February. Today is November 15, 2026, so the current year's bill is already payable and that window is open until the end of February 2027.

The Trustee lists Collierville among the jurisdictions whose taxes become delinquent on March 1. Interest of 1.5% a month, or 18% a year, then starts accruing on the unpaid base tax for Collierville and Shelby County alike. Mailed payments count if they are postmarked on or before the last day of February, and checks go to the Shelby County Trustee at P.O. Box 2751, Memphis, TN 38101-2751 with the detached stub of the notice.

The Trustee's customer service number is (901) 222-0200. Delinquent real estate taxes can lead to a lawsuit in Chancery or Circuit Court under Tenn. Code Ann. 67-5-2405, and a lien cannot be removed until the full balance is paid.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Collierville assessment?
sections.html:
Start with an informal review at the Shelby County Assessor, then file with the Shelby County Board of Equalization if the value still looks wrong. The informal review is not an appeal. It is a chance to give the Assessor sales, photos or an appraisal so the value reflects the market.

Appeal steps and dates for a Collierville home
StepTimingWhere
Informal reviewEnds the last day of MayShelby County Assessor of Property
County board appealUsually ends the last working day of JuneBoard of Equalization, 901-222-7300
State board appealAugust 1, or 45 days after the county notice, whichever is laterState Board of Equalization, 615-401-7883
CourtAfter the administrative stepsShelby County Chancery Court

Sources: Shelby County Assessor, Appeals Process and the state assessment schedule. The 2026 deadlines have passed, so any new dispute belongs to the 2027 cycle.

sections.h2: What documents help in a Collierville value dispute?
sections.html:
The Assessor asks for evidence that points to market value. Strong exhibits for a Collierville house include:

  • Sale prices of similar homes nearby from the two years before the tax year you are appealing.
  • A recent private appraisal.
  • Photos of the exterior and interior that show condition.
  • For commercial or industrial parcels, three years of income and expense figures.

Census QuickFacts puts the median owner-occupied value in Collierville at $485,900 for 2020 to 2024, and 79.9% of housing units are owner-occupied. Use sales from your own neighborhood, since a single median hides a wide spread.

sections.h2: What does Collierville look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Collierville is a town of about 51,909 people in Shelby County, a suburb in the Memphis metropolitan area with its own school district, Collierville Schools. It counted 51,324 residents in 2020, up from 43,965 in 2010.

Jesse R. Collier laid out the settlement in 1836, and the town was rechartered in 1870 after Civil War damage. The old downtown around the square is a listed historic district. Interstate 269, State Route 385 and Poplar Avenue are the main roads.

Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 give the following picture of local households:

  • 18,161 households averaging 2.82 people.
  • Median household income of $138,598.
  • Median gross rent of $1,691.
  • 62.5% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher.
  • An average commute of 25.1 minutes.

Source: Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: Does Collierville's climate and layout matter to a buyer?
sections.html:
Summers in Collierville run hot and damp, winters stay mild, and the town averages roughly 55 inches of rain a year. Wikipedia's climate summary notes that spring is the season with the most thunderstorms, hail and tornadoes, and that the area sits above the Tennessee average for tornado activity.

The Census Bureau counts 36.32 square miles of land in town and about 1,413 people per square mile. If you are selling, expect buyers to ask about the roof and storm history of the house.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Collierville tax when you sell the house?
sections.html:
The unpaid balance is settled at the closing table, so request a payoff from the Shelby County Trustee and the town's tax department before the closing date. The Trustee warns that every tax year's payoff is verified on the day payment is received and that the owner is responsible for fees through that date.

Check the purchase contract and the settlement statement to see who covers the current year's tax.

Behind on payments? Interest from March 1 adds up at 1.5% each month, and a lien stays on the parcel until the balance is cleared, so a payoff figure is the first thing to ask for. The town and the Trustee are the two offices to call.

faqs.q: When are Collierville property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due the first Monday of October and can be paid without interest until the end of February. For the bill now outstanding, that means the deadline falls at the end of February 2027, and March 1 starts the delinquent period.

faqs.q: What is the Collierville town property tax rate?
faqs.a: The town's Taxes page gives $1.62 for each $100 of assessed value. At the state's 25% residential ratio, a $100,000 appraisal yields $405.00 of town tax. Shelby County bills its own rate on top of that.

faqs.q: What interest applies if I pay a Collierville tax bill late?
faqs.a: Interest is 1.5% per month, or 18% per year, beginning March 1 on unpaid base tax. The Shelby County Trustee lists the same rate for Collierville, Arlington, Lakeland, Millington, Memphis and the county itself.

faqs.q: Is the informal review the same as an appeal?
faqs.a: No. The Shelby County Assessor says an informal review is an opportunity to share information so values reflect market value, and it resolves many disputes. The formal appeal goes to the Shelby County Board of Equalization, usually by the last working day of June.

faqs.q: Whom should I call with a Collierville tax question?
faqs.a: Call the town's tax department at 901-457-2281 for town billing, and Shelby County Trustee customer service at (901) 222-0200 for county balances. For value questions, contact the Shelby County Assessor or the Board of Equalization at 901-222-7300.
